transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

I came in because I’ve been feeling… kind of wound up, almost all day. It’s like my body is bracing for something, even when nothing is actually happening. I’ll be sitting at my computer working, just doing normal tasks, and I notice I’m tense, like I can’t quite settle into myself. And then even after dinner, when I’m supposed to be relaxing, I still feel keyed up, like my body hasn’t gotten the message that it’s okay to calm down. It’s not dramatic exactly, but it’s been constant enough that I thought I should talk to someone.
Do you ever get sudden surges of intense fear or discomfort that peak within a few minutes?

I don’t think so… not in the way you’re describing, where it suddenly spikes and peaks really fast. I mean, I do feel uncomfortable and on edge, but it’s more like it builds into the background and just stays there, if that makes sense. It doesn’t usually hit me like a wave all at once where I think, “Oh my gosh, what’s happening?” It’s more constant than sudden.
Did this start after something stressful happened in your life?

Yes, I think it did, or at least that’s when I really started noticing it. It’s been about thirteen months now. My sister is in Arecibo, and she started needing a lot more help from the family around then, more than before. And I guess I didn’t think of it as one big stressful event at the time, more like this ongoing thing that kept expanding, but when I look back, that’s when this whole feeling of being wound up really seemed to begin.
Do you find the worrying hard to control?

Yes… I do. That’s actually one of the things that bothers me most, because I’ll know, logically, that I need to stop going over something, but I can’t seem to just put it down.

Like I’ll be at my computer and I’ll tell myself, “Daniela, enough, focus on this report,” and I really mean it. I’ll try to redirect myself back to work. But then one small thought turns into five more, and suddenly I’m checking messages again, or rereading something, or replaying what could go wrong if I don’t respond the right way. And then I look up and half an hour has gone by, and I haven’t really made progress on what I was supposed to be doing.

It’s not that I want to sit there worrying. I’ll try to talk myself out of it, but it kind of pulls me back in.
Do you find yourself worrying about a lot of different things, not just your sister?

Yes, definitely. My sister is the biggest one, or at least the one that starts it most often, but it doesn’t stay there. My mind sort of jumps tracks. I’ll be thinking about her in Arecibo, and then suddenly I’m thinking, did I forget to send something at work, or did I miss a detail in a report, or is someone waiting on me and I don’t realize it.

And then it can be my husband driving home — like if he’s a little later than I expected, I start imagining traffic or something happening. Or church things, like whether I agreed to help with something and didn’t write it down, or if I’m letting people down. And bills too, even when they’re not due right that second, I’ll start mentally going over what’s coming up and what could go wrong.

It’s like I’m constantly preparing for problems that haven’t even happened yet. I know some of it is probably unnecessary, but my mind keeps moving from one concern to the next.
Have you been worrying like this on most days for at least the past 6 months?

Yes, on most days. It’s been… about thirteen months now, I’d say. It really started around the time my sister in Arecibo began needing a lot more help from the family, and since then it hasn’t really let up. There might be a calmer day here or there, but overall, yes, it’s been going on well over six months.
Have you been feeling more easily fatigued than usual?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean, I do get tired sometimes, but I don’t know if I’d say it’s more than usual or that it stands out as a separate thing.

Some days after being on the computer for hours, I’ll feel worn out, but that could just be the workday, you know? Or just being busy. I haven’t really been keeping track of it in that way. It’s not something I’ve noticed as a major change, at least not like, “Oh, I’m exhausted all the time.” So… I’d say not really, or I’m not sure.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I use a computer for work, so there are times when I’m staring at something and I realize I’ve read the same line more than once, but I don’t know if that’s “trouble concentrating” in the way you mean.

I can usually get through what I need to do. It might take me a little longer if my mind is busy, but I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed some big change where I can’t focus at all. It’s more like… normal distraction, maybe? Or I’ll lose my place and then get back to it. So I’d say not especially, or at least it hasn’t stood out to me as a major problem.
Have you been having muscle tension?

Yes, I think so. That’s actually a big part of why I came in. I feel sort of wound up almost all day, like my body is bracing for something, even when nothing is happening.

Like, I’ll just be sitting at my computer trying to work, and I notice I’m holding myself really stiffly, or I can’t quite settle into the chair. And then after dinner, when I’m supposed to be relaxing, it’s still there — like my body hasn’t gotten the message that it’s okay to let go. It’s not always painful exactly, but it’s this tight, tense feeling, like I’m ready for something bad to happen.
Have you been more irritable than usual?

Yes… I think I have been, though I don’t love admitting that. I’m usually a pretty patient person, or at least I try to be. But lately it’s like my tolerance for little things is thinner than normal.

Like in a documentation meeting, if an update is late or someone hasn’t put something where it’s supposed to go, I’ll hear myself answering more sharply than I intended. Or at choir, if someone is singing off-tempo, I get irritated in a way that feels out of proportion. And then at home, even something simple like cooking on Sunday, if people ask me too many questions while I’m trying to get everything done, I’ll snap a little. Not yelling, exactly, but my tone comes out clipped, and afterward I feel bad because it’s not really how I mean to be.
Do you often feel restless or unable to relax?

Yes. That’s probably one of the main things I notice, honestly. I feel wound up so much of the day, almost like my body is waiting for something to happen even when there’s no actual reason for it.

I’ll be sitting at my computer, just doing normal work, and I realize I’m sort of braced in my chair, like I haven’t settled into it. Or after dinner, when I should be relaxing, I still feel keyed up, like my body hasn’t really turned off. It’s not always dramatic, but it’s there a lot — this restless, tense feeling, like I can’t fully let myself relax.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

Yes, I have. It’s not that I never sleep at all — most nights I do eventually fall asleep — but it doesn’t feel like good, solid sleep.

A lot of nights I’ll wake up around three or four in the morning, and then my brain just sort of turns on. I’ll start thinking about my sister’s next appointment, whether I remembered something I was supposed to do, or some server issue at work that probably can’t even be dealt with at that hour. And I’ll lie there trying to talk myself out of thinking about it, which of course just makes me more aware that I’m awake.

Sometimes I do technically get enough hours, if you just counted them, but I still wake up feeling like I haven’t really rested. Like I’ve been half-working in my sleep or something. So yes, sleep has been... not great.
